A home server that looks after itself.

Sparky is a small box you plug in at home. Tell it what you want running — your own film and TV library, ad blocking for every device in the house, document scanning, home automation — and it installs the software, keeps it updated and backs it up. You ask for things in Telegram, in plain English.

We’ll only use this to let you know when Sparky is available. How we handle your data.

The homelab, without the admin.

Self-hosting gives you your own services instead of someone else’s subscriptions. It usually also gives you a second job. Sparky does that job.

You ask

“Set up a film library I can watch on the TV.”

Sparky installs and configures the stack, puts it behind a name that works on your network, and tells you when it’s ready. No compose files, no port numbers, no wiki.

It runs

Real services, on your hardware.

Plex or Jellyfin, Pi-hole, Home Assistant, Paperless-ngx, Tandoor, n8n and more — the same open source people run by hand, installed and wired up for you.

It maintains

Updates, backups, watching.

Sparky updates itself and the services it installed, takes nightly backups, and restarts what falls over. When something needs a decision, it asks you instead of failing quietly.

It stays yours

The box is in your house, and so is the data.

Your files and services live on the device you own. Nothing needs to leave your home for the homelab to work. If you use the optional managed AI, only those messages pass through Sparky Cloud.

You don’t administer it. You ask it.

Installing, configuring, updating, moving data, adding a service, fixing what broke: all of it happens through a conversation, not a terminal.

It keeps working when you stop paying attention.

A homelab fails slowly, in ways you notice months later. Sparky watches the parts that rot — updates, disk space, backups, dead containers — because that is the part people give up on.

Everything a homelab gives you. None of the evenings it takes.

Tell Sparky what you want running. It handles the rest, and tells you what it did.
